corrected_fields.summary: The Federal Reserve submitted its quarterly Monetary Policy Report to Congress on July 13, 2018, reaffirming its dual mandate: maximum employment and price stability (2% inflation target measured by PCE). Chairman Jerome H. Powell transmitted the report, which outlines the FOMC's commitment to a symmetric inflation goal and the Committee's balanced approach when employment and inflation objectives conflict. The report references the median FOMC estimate of 4.6% as the longer-run normal unemployment rate. Note: Source text captured only the front matter and statement of longer-run goals; substantive economic analysis (Parts 1-3) was truncated and unavailable.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: This quarterly report establishes the foundational policy framework and mandate interpretation that guided Fed decision-making in mid-2018. For macro analysis, it provides the official baseline for how the FOMC thinks about the employment-inflation tradeoff, the symmetric nature of its inflation target, and the uncertainty inherent in estimating maximum employment. Market participants use these documents to understand the Fed's reaction function and policy strategy. [Note: Substantive economic analysis and projections from Parts 1-3 of the report are not available in the source text for verification.]
